read.thesis: Duke is a regulated utility, not a supply-side cyclical: it reaffirmed 2026 EPS $6.55–$6.80 and added $5–10B capex upside tied to 7.8 GW of signed data-centre ESAs, with a 15.4 GW pipeline.

utilisation.quote: Favorable weather has also contributed to our strong results through midyear

capex.quote: there is $5 billion to $10 billion of upside to our current 5-year capital plan to support additional generation and transmission needs

triggers.label: Signed data-centre ESAs 7.8 GW
triggers.quote: We have now secured 7.8 gigawatts of electric service agreements with data center customers.

triggers.label: Capex upside $5–10B
triggers.quote: there is $5 billion to $10 billion of upside to our current 5-year capital plan

triggers.label: 2026 EPS $6.55–$6.80 reaffirmed
triggers.quote: we remain firmly on track to achieve our 2026 guidance range of $6.55 to $6.80.

guidance.quote: we remain firmly on track to achieve our 2026 guidance range of $6.55 to $6.80.
we are more confident than ever that we will deliver in the top half of the range beginning in 2028
We are on track to achieve our FFO to debt target of 14.5% for the year.

red_flags.label: Equity dilution via ATM
red_flags.quote: We've also priced $600 million under the ATM program so far this year, which will settle at the end of 2027.

red_flags.label: Large-load ESA execution risk
red_flags.quote: these negotiations are taking a little longer at times because they're very complicated transactions.

evasions.topic: Timing of 3Q EPS CAGR update / pipeline conversion
evasions.quote: we typically update that in the fourth quarter. But if anything changes materially like we did last year, we'll update you on that as we see fit.
So no real timeline, and we're not putting ourselves under pressure of a timeline.
